## A10 Submission Files

Each file goes in `assignments/assignment10-portfolio-surgery/submission/`.

### `reproducibility-test.md`

Document the fresh-environment test using [port02](port02-fresh-codespace-test.qmd).

- **Verify:** latest commit hash, environment, commands, and result are recorded.

### `failure-log.md`

List failures before repairs. Include warnings, broken paths, missing packages, unclear README steps, citation issues, and stale outputs.

- **Verify:** each failure has evidence and a result after repair or triage.

### `peer-review.md`

Record feedback received or given for M4 readiness. Keep comments specific and actionable.

### `repair-summary.md`

Name the files changed and why. This can be short.

| File changed | Reason | Verification |
|---|---|---|
| `README.md` | Added render command | Followed command in fresh Codespace |

### `final-risk-list.md`

Name remaining risks or state that no known risks remain. Honest risk lists are better than hidden problems.

### `ai-use-note.md`

State what AI helped with and how repairs or wording were checked.

## Final Portfolio Bridge

<!-- AI-EDIT(2026-06-11): TF-035, MIT-104 — needs review -->
The revision target is all of it — the analysis project, the report, the dashboard-style KT product, and the repository with its README — not just one piece.

The final portfolio is not a separate new analysis. It gathers the strongest version of:

- final report source and rendered output;
- dashboard-style KT product or static preview;
- data provenance and stewardship documentation;
- reproducibility instructions;
- presentation slides or presentation summary;
- final AI-use audit;
- clear README and repository access route.

Your dashboard-style KT product may be submitted as a static preview; a live dashboard is not required. <!-- AI-EDIT(2026-06-11): WI-075 (R2-07) — needs review -->

Use the [Final Portfolio Checklist](../../milestones/final-portfolio/final-portfolio-checklist.md) before submission.

<!-- AI-EDIT(2026-06-11): GAP-R911-3 (R2-11), GAP-R911-4 (R2-12) — needs review -->
Two rules make this easier:

- **You may revise earlier work — and you are encouraged to.** If feedback on an earlier assignment showed you a better way, fix it before it goes into the portfolio. The portfolio is graded on the strongest version of your work, not the first version you submitted.
- **Required files are prescribed; the rest of the structure is yours.** The checklist names the files every portfolio must contain. Beyond those files, your group is free to organize and present the portfolio however serves your project best.

<!-- AI-EDIT(2026-06-11): TF-037, MIT-105 — needs review -->
Not sure what "strong" looks like? A weak portfolio is a pile of files the reader must decode. A strong portfolio leads with a README that answers what the project is, who it is for, what was found, and how to rerun it. See the side-by-side [weak vs strong README example](port03-readme-repo-hygiene.qmd#weak-vs-strong-a-readme-example).

## Public or Private Repository

Use [Repository Sharing Guidance](../../milestones/final-portfolio/repository-sharing-guidance.md). Private repositories are appropriate when public sharing would create data, privacy, licensing, or stewardship risk.

Public is not better by default. Reviewable, safe, and reproducible is the target.

## Before Submitting A10

Check:

- fresh environment test attempted;
- failures logged before repair;
- report and KT product rerun or failure clearly explained;
- README matches the tested workflow;
- M4 feedback is recorded;
- final risk list is honest;
- required files are committed and synced.

## Before Final Portfolio

After A10, focus on:

- repairing remaining blockers;
- aligning presentation slides with final report claims;
- checking repository access;
- confirming public/private sharing choice;
- syncing the final commit before Canvas submission.
